title: Rebuild an old game's source code with AI models
summary: A developer used OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models to reconstruct Civilization 1's source; it builds with 1991-era tools into a byte-for-byte match, apart from a four-byte fix.
agent_role: The AI models wrote the reconstructed code and documentation, guided to use earlier OpenCiv1 work; the developer edited the results and set up build checks against the original program.
outcome: Author reports the rebuilt CIV.EXE matches version 474.05 byte for byte, aside from a checked four-byte startup correction.
what_they_did: A developer directed AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to turn the 1991 Civilization program back into readable C code. He pointed them at an earlier project, OpenCiv1, then edited the output. He built it with the original-era Microsoft compiler in an emulator and checked the result against the real game file. The AI also helped write a technical book about the game.
how_it_went: He reports the rebuilt program matches the original byte for byte, except a four-byte fix for a likely post-build patch. He also used the code to make a modern version of the game.
worth_knowing: The author credits OpenCiv1 with most of the work and warns the names and comments are guesses, so a matching program does not prove this is the original source.
prompt: Help me reconstruct readable source code for [old program name and version]. Use [existing reverse-engineering project or notes] as a starting point. Work one function at a time: write the code, build it with [period compiler/toolchain], and compare the output with the original file. Keep a log of which parts match and which don't. Show me your plan first and pause after each batch of functions for my review.

curation.rationale: A developer used AI models to rebuild Civilization's 1991 source code so it compiles to a byte-identical game, with public code, checks and a book. Novel and verifiable, though the AI's exact workflow is only briefly described.
